question: Should OpenClaw change `contextPruning.ttl` to expire or summarize normal conversation history, keep TTL pruning tool-result-only and document the supported reset/compact controls, or add a separate authorized session/context prune contract?
rationale: The remaining work changes documented retention semantics and may add privileged session mutation APIs, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Design a typed session/context contract
options.body: Define prune, compact, reset, TTL/rolling retention, authorization, persistence, summary, and recovery semantics before implementing any endpoint.

options.title: Document current behavior only
options.body: Keep cache-TTL pruning tool-result-only and clarify that users should use `/compact`, `/new`, `/reset`, and `sessions.reset` for supported controls.

options.title: Retarget TTL to conversation history
options.body: Make TTL expire or summarize normal messages, accepting a compatibility-sensitive change to transcript retention semantics with migration and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Design a typed session/context contract
recommendation.body: Define prune, compact, reset, TTL/rolling retention, authorization, persistence, summary, and recovery semantics before implementing any endpoint.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the latest reviewer on this issue and has recent history on both cache-TTL pruning and the public session/pruning docs.
